\title{Elicit vs.\ Teach, Mechanistically: Results on the TinyStories-1B Twins}
\author{MARS V --- Mechanistic Understanding of Elicitation vs.\ Teaching}
\date{Working results document, September 2026}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\section*{Setup}

Two identical TinyStories-1B twins (same architecture, same pretraining on
children's stories, zero arithmetic) are fine-tuned on the same target task
--- signed 1--4-digit addition/subtraction in natural language,
\texttt{What is the difference between 8 and 5784?}$\;\to\;$\texttt{-5776} ---
with one byte-held protocol (LoRA $r{=}512$, $\alpha{=}32$, lr $3.53{\times}10^{-4}$,
batch 128, seed 316, eps/k convergence stop, frozen D\_algo\_bare, $n = 10^2\ldots10^6$).
The arms differ \emph{only} in the parent checkpoint:

\begin{itemize}[nosep]
  \item \textbf{Teach twin}: the blank base (\texttt{evt-ts1b-base}). The capability is absent.
  \item \textbf{Elicit twin}: \textbf{TS1B-latent} (\texttt{evt-ts1b-op-bridge-mix}) --- the blank base
    plus (i) a symbol-only arithmetic install (\texttt{23 + 45 = 68}, 1M examples, full FT) and
    (ii) an answer-free word$\leftrightarrow$symbol binding dose (rewriting
    \texttt{What is the sum of 621 and 5068?} $\leftrightarrow$ \texttt{621 + 5068}, rehearsed 1:1
    with already-seen symbol rows). Every installation is answer-free and leakage-controlled
    (Table~\ref{tab:premise}). The capability is latent.
\end{itemize}

\noindent\textbf{Measurement vocabulary.}
\emph{Circuit} = top-32 of 528 nodes (512 attention heads + 16 MLP outputs) by attribution
score (gradient of the clean/corrupt logit-diff $\times$ activation delta, 128--256 pairs);
overlaps are Jaccard@32 against a chance floor of 0.031 and a per-map split-half ceiling.
\emph{Weight write} = $\Delta W = \text{scaling}\cdot BA$ per LoRA module (exact; singular
values via thin QR); total write $\|\Delta W\|_F$, relative write $\|\Delta W\|/\|W\|$,
travel $\|\Delta W_t\|_F$ and speed $\|\Delta W_t-\Delta W_{t-1}\|_F/\Delta t$ from adapter
snapshots (the measurable form of ``gradient strength'' under AdamW, whose updates are
$\sqrt{v}$-normalised).

\begin{table}[h]\centering\small
\begin{tabular}{lcc}
\toprule
Construction step / check & value & control \\
\midrule
symbol install: EM on \texttt{23 + 45 = } & 0.67--0.73 & blank: 0.00 \\
corpus census: ``sum'' in 439M words & 21$\times$ & ``equals'' 17, ``minus'' 57 \\
binding dose: NL$\to$op rewrite exact & 0.484 & blank + dose: 0.000 EM \\
sum-only dose on \emph{difference} questions & writes ``+'' & per-word binding \\
\textbf{direct NL exact match of the parent} & \textbf{0.000} & $=$ blank twin \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{The latent parent is behaviorally identical to the blank twin on the target task.
Everything below is about what differs inside.}
\label{tab:premise}
\end{table}

\section*{Results}

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{R\arabic*}, leftmargin=*, itemsep=1.2em]

% ------------------------------------------------------------------ R1
\item \textbf{The learning-curve signature flips.}
\metric{Prequential EDL per label token (nats) and held-out exact match, as a function of
dataset size $n$, identical protocol, parent varied.}
\result{Figure~\ref{fig:flip}, Table~\ref{tab:sweep}. Elicit: EDL strictly monotone,
$4.53\to0.092$; EM $0.54$ at $n{=}3{,}162$, $0.98$ at $1$M. Teach: EDL down--up--down with the
hump peaking near $n{=}215$K; EM $0.093$ at $1$M. EM-0.5 threshold: $\sim\!3\times10^3$ vs
$>10^6$ ($>300\times$). A third arm (blank + format-only dose) keeps its hump.}
\interp{Eliciting spends every example connecting an existing capability (diminishing cost from
the first rung); teaching must build the capability, producing increasing returns mid-run.
The flip is the paper's causal-intervention claim reproduced on one substrate, with a parent
whose latency is itemised rather than assumed.}
\begin{figure}[h]\centering
\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{02_learning_curves/fig_signature_flip.png}
\caption{EDL/token (left) and 0-shot EM (right) vs $n$; teal = teach twin, gold = elicit twin.}
\label{fig:flip}
\end{figure}
\begin{table}[h]\centering\small
\begin{tabular}{rcccc}
\toprule
$n$ & \multicolumn{2}{c}{elicit} & \multicolumn{2}{c}{teach} \\
 & EDL/tok & EM & EDL/tok & EM \\
\midrule
100 & 4.533 & 0.023 & 6.511 & 0.007 \\
316 & 4.208 & 0.038 & 6.387 & 0.033 \\
1{,}000 & 3.579 & 0.155 & $\sim$4.9 & $\sim$0 \\
3{,}162 & 3.168 & \textbf{0.541} & $\downarrow$ & $\sim$0 \\
10{,}000 & 2.444 & 0.743 & min $\sim$0.8 & $\sim$0 \\
31{,}623 & 1.137 & 0.867 & $\uparrow$ & $\sim$0 \\
100{,}000 & 0.467 & 0.915 & $\uparrow$ & $\sim$0 \\
316{,}228 & 0.215 & 0.966 & peak $\sim$2.0 @215K & $\sim$0 \\
1{,}000{,}000 & \textbf{0.092} & \textbf{0.981} & 1.40 & 0.093 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{Per-rung values (EDL nats/label token; EM on 1,024 held-out problems).}
\label{tab:sweep}

% ------------------------------------------------------------------ R2
\item \textbf{The elicited circuit is the parent's installed circuit; the taught circuit
matches nothing upstream.}
\metric{Jaccard@32 between attribution circuits (chance 0.031; ceiling = split-half
self-agreement of the map, 0.684 for the elicited child).}
\result{Table~\ref{tab:overlap}. Parent (installed engine) $\leftrightarrow$ elicited child:
$0.455$--$0.524$ across eval surfaces ($\approx$70\% of ceiling), top-4 nodes identical and
identically ordered (\texttt{mlp:15,14,13,12}). Blank parent: no measurable circuit (logit-diff
$-0.33$ even 16-shot; its map is noise), so the taught child has nothing to match.}
\interp{Elicitation re-weights machinery that was already there; teaching constructs machinery
where there was none. ``Reuse'' is measured, not inferred.}
\begin{table}[h]\centering\small
\begin{tabular}{lccc}
\toprule
Comparison & J@32 & chance & ceiling \\
\midrule
installed engine $\leftrightarrow$ elicited child (op / bridge surface) & 0.455--0.488 / 0.524 & 0.031 & 0.684 \\
blank parent $\leftrightarrow$ taught child & undefined (parent map is noise) & -- & -- \\
elicited child @3K $\leftrightarrow$ @1M & 0.391 & 0.031 & 0.684 \\
elicited child @1M $\leftrightarrow$ taught child @1M & 0.231 (Spearman $-0.11$) & 0.031 & 0.684 / 0.561 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{Circuit-membership overlaps. All maps pass the performing-regime guard.}
\label{tab:overlap}
\end{table}

% ------------------------------------------------------------------ R3
\item \textbf{Same task, same substrate, different machine.}
\metric{Layer distribution of the top-16 attribution nodes; J@32 and score Spearman between
the two children.}
\result{Figure~\ref{fig:layers}. Elicited child: mid/late MLP backbone (layers 5--15) plus the
layer-7 attention trio --- the installed engine's own profile. Taught child: eight layer-0
attention heads over raw digit tokens feeding a few late MLPs. Overlap $0.231$, score
correlation $-0.11$.}
\interp{Because both children share the identical pretrained substrate, the mechanism
difference is caused by the learning regime alone --- the cross-model version of this finding
had a pretraining confound; this one does not.}
\begin{figure}[h]\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.9\textwidth]{03_circuits/fig_layer_profile_ts.png}
\caption{Top-16 node layer histograms (solid = MLP, hatched = attention) for the installed engine, the elicited child, and the taught child.}
\label{fig:layers}
\end{figure}

% ------------------------------------------------------------------ R4
\item \textbf{The elicited circuit exists before training; the taught circuit is built
mid-run --- through the EDL hump.}
\metric{Jaccard@32 of each training snapshot's circuit against the run's final circuit.}
\result{Figure~\ref{fig:form}. Elicit: $0.488$ at step 1 (16$\times$ chance), a brief
interface-wiring transient (dip to $\sim$0.42 with a strong map at step 154), locked from
$\sim$step 1.5K of 11.5K ($0.561$; 82\% of ceiling, 97\% of the J@64 ceiling by 8.4K). Teach:
noise floor ($\approx$0.22--0.28) until $\sim$step 1.3K, then $0.27\to0.44$ over steps
1.3K--5.4K --- the region where its EDL peaks.}
\interp{Elicitation finds and wires; teaching constructs. The elicited circuit finishes
stabilising before the taught one begins to exist, and the teaching hump is literally the
circuit being assembled.}
\begin{figure}[h]\centering
\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{03_circuits/fig_formation_ts.png}
\caption{Circuit formation, elicit (left) vs teach (right); dashed = split-half ceiling.}
\label{fig:form}
\end{figure}

% ------------------------------------------------------------------ R5
\item \textbf{The words reach the engine only when the binding is installed.}
\metric{Cross-format activation matching: per node, mean cosine between the activation on the
NL rendering and on the symbol rendering of the \emph{same} problem, minus the mismatched-pair
baseline (``does \texttt{What is the sum of 621 and 5068?} drive the node into the same
problem-specific state as \texttt{621 + 5068 = }?'').}
\result{Engine without binding: MLP index $\approx0.00$--$0.01$ at every layer. TS1B-latent
(binding installed): $+0.07$--$0.13$ across layers 7--15, $\sim$10$\times$. Attention-head
indices are confounded by shared digit tokens and are excluded.}
\interp{This is what ``latent'' means internally: before any target training, NL input already
activates the arithmetic MLPs of the elicit parent, while the teach parent has no arithmetic
MLPs to activate. It also shows the binding dose did what it claimed --- installed an access
route, not the task.}

% ------------------------------------------------------------------ R6
\item \textbf{The latent capability can be reached with frozen weights; the absent one cannot.}
\metric{Exact match on the target task under zero-training interventions: (a) self-chain ---
the model rewrites the question itself, then computes its own rewrite; (b) donor patching ---
the fine-tuned child's activations at the 32 circuit nodes written into the parent (mean
vector, or per-prompt states); random-node controls.}
\result{Figure~\ref{fig:ladder}, Table~\ref{tab:steer}. Elicit parent: direct $0.000\to$
self-chain $\mathbf{0.328}$ ($=0.484\times0.668$; the composition law parse$\times$compute held on
four model variants); per-prompt states $0.125$ (random nodes: $0.000$); mean vector: format
only. Teach side: blank + same doses $0.000$; blank + chain $0.000$ (a parser without an
engine); taught donor into blank twin $0.000$ in every condition.}
\interp{Elicit = one composition step or one state-patch away from the target; teach = nothing
underneath to switch on. The teach-side nulls double as the leakage control for the whole
construction.}
\begin{figure}[h]\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.55\textwidth]{04_interventions/fig_intervention_ladder.png}
\caption{Intervention ladder on the elicit parent (weights frozen except the last bar).}
\label{fig:ladder}
\end{figure}
\begin{table}[h]\centering\small
\begin{tabular}{llcc}
\toprule
Patient + intervention (k=32 circuit nodes) & condition & format & EM \\
\midrule
TS1B-latent + child mean shift & circuit nodes & 0.164 & 0.000 \\
TS1B-latent + child per-prompt states & circuit nodes & 0.359 & \textbf{0.125} \\
 & random-32 nodes & 0.051 & 0.000 \\
TS1B-latent self-chain (no donor) & own rewrite + ``= '' & -- & \textbf{0.328} \\
blank + binding dose, self-chain & parser without engine & -- & 0.000 \\
blank + taught donor & every condition & 0.000 & 0.000 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{Zero-training interventions, TinyStories twins.}
\label{tab:steer}
\end{table}

% ------------------------------------------------------------------ R7
\item \textbf{Teaching writes far more into the weights, and buys far less per unit written.}
\metric{Relative write $\|\Delta W\|/\|W\|$ (exact from LoRA factors); total travel and per-step
speed from adapter snapshots; capability per unit travel = final EM / total travel.}
\result{Table~\ref{tab:weights}, Figure~\ref{fig:travel}. Relative write $0.212$ (teach) vs
$0.095$ (elicit), $2.2\times$; total travel $457$ vs $120$, $3.8\times$, over $2\times$ as many
steps (23.5K vs 11.5K); capability per unit travel $2.0\times10^{-4}$ vs $8.1\times10^{-3}$,
$\sim$40$\times$.}
\interp{Eliciting connects what exists; teaching writes what does not. The temporal
\emph{shape} of writing (burst then decay) is shared by both arms --- an optimisation
signature --- so the discrimination is in amplitude, duration, and efficiency, not timing.}
\begin{table}[h]\centering\small
\begin{tabular}{lcc}
\toprule
 & elicit (TS1B-latent) & teach (blank) \\
\midrule
relative write $\|\Delta W\|/\|W\|$ (1M) & 0.095 & 0.212 \\
steps to convergence & 11{,}500 & 23{,}496 \\
peak / final writing speed (per step) & 0.218 / 0.018 & 0.306 / 0.022 \\
total weight travel $\|\Delta W\|_F$ & 120 & 457 \\
final exact match & 0.981 & 0.093 \\
capability per unit travel & $8.1\times10^{-3}$ & $2.0\times10^{-4}$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{Weight-space write, elicit vs teach.}
\label{tab:weights}
\end{table}
\begin{figure}[h]\centering
\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{05_weights/fig_weight_travel.png}
\caption{Weight travel (left) and speed (right) from adapter snapshots; profiles coincide, amplitudes do not.}
\label{fig:travel}
\end{figure}

% ------------------------------------------------------------------ R8
\item \textbf{The regime difference is total: the two children differ at both node and edge
level.}
\metric{$\Delta S = 1-\text{Jaccard}$ at node level (@32) and edge level (@256, node$\to$block
edge attribution).}
\result{Elicited @1M vs taught @1M: $\Delta S_{\text{node}} = 0.769$, $\Delta S_{\text{edge}} =
0.739$ (ratio 0.96), both far above the noise floors (0.32 / 0.61).}
\interp{When the mechanism differs, it differs everywhere --- membership and wiring alike ---
consistent with R3: not a re-routed version of one machine but two machines.}

\end{enumerate}

\section*{Validation results (not regime differences, but what licenses R2--R6)}

\begin{itemize}[nosep]
  \item \textbf{Both circuits are real and load-bearing.} True activation patching: elicited child
    top-8 of 528 nodes $=0.997$ sufficient / $0.998$ necessary (top-32: $0.999$ / $1.000$);
    taught child top-8 necessity $0.986$, top-32 $\sim$0.999. Every overlap above compares
    provably load-bearing sets.
  \item \textbf{Construction controls.} Identical doses on the blank twin change nothing on the
    target (0.000 in every probe); a sum-only binding dose leaves ``difference'' unbound (per-word
    binding); the composition law chain $=$ parse $\times$ compute held on four variants.
\end{itemize}

\section*{Informative non-discriminators (measured, reported for completeness)}

\begin{itemize}[nosep]
  \item Effective rank of $\Delta W$ (participation ratio): elicit 7.1, teach 5.2 of 512 ---
    both energy-concentrated; rank does not separate the regimes. Alignment of $\Delta W$ with
    the base's top-64 singular directions is near the 0.058 baseline for both.
  \item Temporal profile of weight travel: burst-then-decay in both arms (R7).
  \item Prompt brittleness (16-shot collapse) is a property of this lineage's training-sequence
    structure, not of the regime: both children score $\sim$0 at 16 shots.
  \item Edge-level $\Delta S$ within the elicit arm: the edge instrument's split-half noise
    floor (0.61--0.62) exceeds the measured churn on both eval surfaces --- a sensitivity limit.
\end{itemize}
